message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to current air‑quality data, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  
If you’d like up‑to‑date information, you can check one of the following:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (airnow.gov) | Enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code to see the latest AQI and pollutant levels. |
| **EPA’s Air Quality Index** (aqicn.org) | Search for “Los Angeles” or use the map to view real‑time data. |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather) | Many include an AQI widget for major cities. |
| **Local news sites** | They often report on smog alerts and health advisories. |

In general, Los Angeles can experience moderate to unhealthy air quality on hot, dry days when temperature inversions trap pollutants near the surface. If you’re planning outdoor activities, it’s a good idea to check the current AQI and any health advisories before heading out.
